limitations: Actual selected events came from a history RPC while opening the chat; real live new/edit/delete events were not observed.
Append, restart, rotation, duplicates and edit/delete logic are qualified only against synthetic fixtures in this spike.
Diagnostic transport records do not prove Telegram application acceptance, complete history or gap-free delivery.
Unsupported packet/update and incomplete-history outcomes remain visible in the private journal.
One account only; no account switching, media download, AI handoff or TGSUM GUI integration.
Private output assumes no concurrent same-user path replacement or file mutation; publication must be hardened before unattended collection.
Raw source logs contain all client traffic before selected-peer filtering and remain private on disk; no deletion or retention change was performed.
Full workspace checks retain existing opt-in ignored sandbox tests; they do not expand this experimental source qualification.
rollback: Gracefully quit the debug instance, wait for exit, then restore the exact original Telegram launch without -debug; verified for this stable client with initially absent persistent debug setting. Source logs and selected journal remain on disk.
